articles.title: US stocks slide: Amazon, Intel, Nvidia fall
articles.summary: US stock market today: US stocks fell for the second day in a row on Friday, October 30, as investors worried about the health of the AI trade. At 10:58 AM ET, the Dow Jones was at 52,113.50, down 229.06 points or 0.44%. The S&P 500 was at 7,621.06, down 99.33 points or 1.29%. The Nasdaq was at 25,623.29, down 561.44 points or 2.14%.Why is the US stock market down today?Two earnings reports, from Amazon and Intel, came after Thursday’s closing bell and are pulling the market down this morning.Thursday was already weak. All three major indexes closed lower, and the Nasdaq lost 1.6% after Alphabet’s results disappointed. Amazon and Alphabet both posted rare earnings misses. Alphabet had its worst day in over 20 years.Amazon missed estimates on both revenue and profit. Its free cash flow also fell because of heavy spending on AI. Intel dropped sharply after giving a weak outlook for the fourth quarter.Chip stocks fell across the board. AMD lost 9%, Marvell 6% and Broadcom 5%. Micron and Nvidia each gave up more than 3%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), which holds Intel and AMD as its two biggest positions, was down 7%.Crypto stocks also took a hit. Bitcoin fell to around $76,600 from a high near $82,000 on Thursday. Strategy (MSTR) was down 10%, Coinbase (COIN) 12% and Robinhood (HOOD) 8%.In other markets, WTI crude was above $104 a barrel, up about 2%. Gold fell to around $3,920, close to its lowest level since last November. The 10-year Treasury yield stayed at 4.94%.Intel stock price today: why the chipmaker is down nearly 30%Intel (INTC) is the worst performer on the S&P 500 today. At 10:58 AM ET it traded at $66.52, down $25.55 or 27.75%. Earlier in the session it fell about 30%, to below $65. That is a price the stock has not seen since spring.The fall comes after a big run. Intel was up roughly 250% this year through Thursday’s close, and had recently crossed levels last seen in 2000.The trigger was the company’s outlook. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and GAAP profit of 10 cents a share. Both are below the average estimate tracked by Visible Alpha. This overshadowed third-quarter numbers that were better than expected. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company faces “headwinds across the PC industry” and is finding it hard to meet “extremely high AI driven demand.”Intel’s foundry business, which makes chips for other companies, is also under watch. Its revenue rose nearly 60% year on year in Q3, but it posted an operating loss of nearly $1.9 billion.Valuation is another worry. Before the fall, Intel traded at more than 50 times estimated 2027 earnings, well above its peer group average. Morgan Stanley, which rates the stock neutral, cut its price target to $75 from $84. The Visible Alpha average target is around $90.High trending stocks today: Amazon, Nvidia, Reddit and moreAmazon (AMZN) traded at $239.31, down 1.84%. Third-quarter revenue rose nearly 12% from a year ago to about $202 billion. Net income fell, partly because last year’s quarter had gains from its stake in Anthropic. Amazon still expects AWS revenue growth run rates above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. The stock is up just 3% this year, while the S&P 500 is up 11%.Nvidia (NVDA) was at $207.25, down 3%. Alphabet (GOOGL) was at $280.64, down 1.12%, and CoreWeave (CRWV) was at $55.48, down 8.65%. SpaceX (SPCX) was at $138.52, down 3.73%, and Nokia (NOK) was at $8.66, down 6.98%.Three internet stocks also fell after their Q3 results. Reddit (RDDT) dropped 24%, Roblox (RBLX) 16% and Pinterest (PINS) 6%.Acumen Pharmaceuticals (ABOS) fell 87.47% to $0.29.A few stocks rose. TNL Mediagene (TNMG) gained 24.26% to $3.79 and Rivian (RIVN) added 5.41% to $12.07.

articles.title: Binance’s $6.3B crypto heist: Who’s behind it?
articles.summary: Binance hack: Hackers linked to North Korea are the main suspects in the theft of about $6.36 billion from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange. US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs says the group is TraderTraitor, which it calls North Korea’s elite hacking unit. Binance has not confirmed this yet.Who is behind the Binance hack?TRM Labs published its findings on Thursday. It says the attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in around 20 minutes. If the figure holds, this is the largest crypto theft on record.Investigation update: Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach. This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it. We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them.Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe.We are still on track towards the expected timeline to resume the withdrawal service in 45 hours. Deposits remain unaffected.The outflows ceased when we paused withdrawal service earlier. We are still working with partners to freeze many of the impacted assets, and have frozen around $3 billion thus far.We will continue to provide further updates through official Binance channels as more verified information becomes available.— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026TRM says it blames TraderTraitor “with high confidence,” based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. It also says several features of the attack match earlier North Korea-linked thefts, including the Bybit hack.Chainalysis, another blockchain analytics firm, has a similar view. Its co-founder and CEO, Jonathan Levin, wrote on X that the hack was likely done by TraderTraitor.Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea. https://t.co/NIX65d8FpF— USA TODAY (@USATODAY) October 30, 2026Binance has not named anyone. A company spokesperson said only that it is working with law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice.Is TraderTraitor a state-backed group?TRM describes TraderTraitor as a unit of North Korea, which would make it state-backed. No government has confirmed its role in the Binance case so far. The link comes from private security firms.The Bybit case offers some background. In February last year, Bybit lost $1.5 billion in a hack. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible.Experts say North Korea turned to crypto theft because it needs foreign currency. Strict UN sanctions have hurt its economy, and the money is believed to help fund its nuclear programme.In December 2022, South Korea’s spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen around $1.1 billion in crypto and other digital assets in the previous five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone.How the theft happened and what Binance says nowBinance first said the attacker may have got in through a compromised laptop belonging to an employee or contractor, which allowed unauthorised withdrawal requests. A later check found more “points of breach,” the company said. It also said it found no evidence that any wallet private key had leaked.Kok Tin Gan, CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab, believes a single signature may have given the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet. A hot wallet is one connected to the internet. He questioned why stronger approval controls were not in place.Binance says it froze roughly $3 billion of the affected assets with help from blockchain partners. Deposits were not affected. Withdrawals are suspended and should resume in a day or two.The company says it will cover all losses and will share more technical details once its investigation ends.Changpeng Zhao, who founded Binance, posted on X that “User funds are safe!” He said it does look like a hack, and that as a shareholder he expects all funds to be fully covered. Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to a felony linked to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

articles.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has warned that a Democratic sweep of the US House of Representatives, Senate and presidency in 2028 could bring major changes to the country’s political system.In a post on X on Thursday, Musk said such an outcome would be “game over for America” and urged voters to support Republican Senate candidates in the November 3 midterm elections.“My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will: Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate; Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority; Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority,” Musk said.— elonmusk (@elonmusk) “This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word,” he said.“All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one,” Musk added.His remarks came as he emerged as the largest individual political donor in US history, having spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the midterm elections.The Hill reported that Musk contributed an additional $76.8 million to his America PAC over the past month. The contribution took his total spending on the upcoming elections beyond $442 million. America PAC received the funds over about a week in October.Musk had already spent $366 million supporting Republican candidates and groups. He established America PAC during the 2024 election cycle.According to campaign finance filings cited by CBS News, Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund through two contributions in September. The super PAC supports Republican Senate candidates and later transferred the money to a Texas-based political action committee backing Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.Musk donated $75 million on September 9 and another $83 million about two weeks later. The contributions accounted for more than half of the Senate Leadership Fund’s receipts in the third quarter, CBS News reported.He also donated $10 million to the pro-Paxton Lone Star Liberty PAC through his trust. In addition, Musk gave $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, $10 million to the Republican Governors Association and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association.The Texas Senate race is among the closely contested contests where Musk has directed his political spending. Republican candidate and state Attorney General Ken Paxton is facing Democratic challenger James Talarico.Musk’s America PAC has also supported Republican candidates in competitive congressional races.His latest spending marks a return to large-scale political donations after he spent more than $250 million supporting President Donald Trump and other Republican candidates during the 2024 election cycle. His involvement had appeared uncertain after his public feud with Trump last year.The November 3 midterm elections will decide control of both chambers of Congress and could determine the future of Trump’s legislative agenda.A CBS News poll published on October 25 projected that Democrats could win 229 seats in the House as inflation and economic concerns influence voters. The estimate could extend into the 230s, although Republicans retain a narrow path to holding the majority.The Democratic lead has remained steady in recent weeks, but CBS News said there was no growing electoral wave.Trump said on October 27 that he would respect the results of the midterm elections if they were conducted honestly, while warning that he could use his veto power if necessary.“We'll figure a way. I have a strong veto. I hope that won't be the case, but if it is, that's happened before… I will — if they're honest elections,” Trump told reporters.The election comes as the administration faces economic concerns and declining approval ratings. The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Trump’s approval rating had fallen to 37%, the lowest recorded for a president approaching midterm elections in the publication’s polling history dating back to 1990.

articles.title: Trump's grip on Congress may be slipping
articles.summary: Donald Trump's grip on Congress is starting to look a little shaky. Four days before the US midterm elections, major polls show Democrats with a clear national advantage in the fight for the House of Representatives. The Senate remains more competitive, but new CNN polling has put Democrats ahead in several key races that could decide control of the chamber.Also Read| What's at stake for Trump, his opponents and 2028 White House raceRepublicans currently control both chambers of Congress. Democrats need a net gain of three seats in the House and four in the Senate to take control.US Midterm Elections 2026: What do the latest polls reveal?The latest surveys from major news organisations and pollsters show Democrats leading the national congressional ballot by 8 to 10 percentage points.PollField datesDemocratic leadReuters/IpsosOct 22–2653% to 44% — D+9CBS News/YouGovOct 21–2353% to 45% — D+8NPR/PBS News/MaristOct 19–2052% to 44% — D+8CNN/SSRSOct 15–1849% to 39% — D+10ABC News/Washington Post/IpsosOct 9–1352% to 44% — D+8AP-NORCOct 8–1247% to 38% — D+9The latest national poll in this group is the Reuters/Ipsos survey, which interviewed voters through October 26. The AP-NORC, ABC News/Washington Post and CNN national polls were conducted earlier and should not be read as a measure of voter sentiment on October 30.The AP-NORC poll found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who wanted Republicans to remain in charge. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos survey found an even wider preference for Democratic control: 59% wanted the next Congress to act as a check on Trump, while 35% preferred Republicans to support his agenda.Trump's Approval Rating: How are American voters viewing the President?Trump's approval rating is weak across the major surveys. AP-NORC found that 36% voters approved of his job performance, while 64% disapproved. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll recorded 33% approval and 66% disapproval.The Reuters/Ipsos poll, conducted most recently, put Trump’s approval at 32%. Only 25% approved of his handling of the economy and 20% approved of his handling of the cost of living.Economic concerns are central to the election. In the AP-NORC poll, 85% of voters called the economy an important issue when deciding how to vote, while 84% said the same about the cost of living.The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll found that 44% of likely voters viewed their congressional vote mainly as a vote against Trump. Only 21% said their vote was mainly in favour of him.CNN polling shows Democratic path to Senate majorityThe Senate remains harder for Democrats because they must win several Republican-leaning states. CNN’s latest battleground polls, released on October 29, showed Democrats ahead in four important Senate races:Texas: James Talarico led Ken Paxton, 49% to 43%.Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed led Mike Rogers, 49% to 42%.Kansas: Adam Hamilton led Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, 49% to 45%.Maine: Troy Jackson led Republican incumbent Susan Collins, 49% to 45%.The Kansas and Maine leads were within the margin of error. The Texas and Michigan results gave Democrats a stronger advantage, although neither race was certain. The CNN results give Democrats a possible route to the four Senate gains they need. But they would still have to perform strongly in other closely contested races, including Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and South Carolina.Republicans have an advantage in the Senate map because several competitive seats are in states Trump carried in 2024. Democrats therefore need to win multiple races where the presidential vote favoured the Republican Party.Also Read| Are educated Republican districts going extinct?House is more favourable to DemocratsCBS News’ latest House model, based on its October 21–23 poll and district-level data, put Democrats on course to win 229 seats. It said Republicans still had a narrow path to retain control.The model also warned that the Democratic lead had not expanded in recent weeks and that voters who were uncertain about voting tended to lean more Republican.That makes turnout critical. Reuters/Ipsos found that 46% of Democrats were very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 30% of Republicans. The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll also found higher overall enthusiasm among Democratic likely voters.Reading the tea leavesThe latest major national polls point to Democratic gains and put the House within the party’s reach. The Senate remains unsettled, but CNN’s newest battleground surveys show Democrats with a possible path to a majority.The numbers do not guarantee a Democratic sweep. The result will depend on turnout, late-deciding voters and whether Democratic candidates can convert narrow leads in Republican-leaning states into victories.

articles.title: India remains growth engine; Super El Nino impact yet to materialise: IMF
articles.summary:
The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy.
The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino.
"So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here.
She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise.
Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July.
